headline: Contracts surge. Funding flows. Space gets serious.
deck: This week saw major contracts awarded and funding rounds that underscore the growing seriousness of the space sector.

stories.head: Sphinx Defense bags $287 million for satellite software
stories.body: Sphinx Defense has secured a $287 million contract to develop strategic satellite communications software, highlighting the increasing complexity of satellite operations. This contract reflects a broader trend where software is becoming just as critical as hardware in space missions. It's a reminder that in space, the software might just be the new rocket fuel.
stories.soWhat: As satellite operations grow more intricate, the demand for advanced software solutions will only intensify, making Sphinx Defense a key player in this evolving market.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million amid defense pull
stories.body: True Anomaly has closed a $190 million Series C funding round, now valued at $1.6 billion, focusing on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. This funding is indicative of a broader defense interest in ensuring space security, especially as tensions rise. In a world where space is becoming the next battleground, True Anomaly is positioning itself well.
stories.soWhat: The influx of capital into space security suggests that the defense sector is recognizing the strategic importance of space, which could lead to further investment and innovation.

stories.head: Intel unveils new chip for space computing
stories.body: Intel has introduced a new chip designed for space computing, aiming to enhance processing power in extreme environments. While the exact specifications remain under wraps, this move could significantly improve onboard data processing capabilities for satellites and other space vehicles. It's a strong signal that even semiconductor giants see a future in the cosmos.
stories.soWhat: As space missions require more sophisticated computing, Intel's push into this market could reshape the competitive landscape, potentially sidelining smaller chipmakers.

watchlist.title: Upper C-band auction results expected
watchlist.body: The results of the Upper C-band auction could reshape the GEO industry landscape, with significant implications for frequency allocations.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris bid outcome
watchlist.body: The outcome of Anduril and L3Harris' tactical SDA constellation bid will reveal how seriously the military is investing in space-based capabilities.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's next steps post-review
watchlist.body: With Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant clearing its critical design review, attention will shift to its timeline for production and potential customers.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program signals confidence in long-term military contracts, which may affect future funding rounds.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
